record.eligibility: Members of the Baylor St. Luke's Medical Center (BSLMC) professional hospital staff or associated investigators may submit proposals. Health care professionals from other institutions are also invited if the project is a collaborative one involving St. Luke's staff, and clinical investigations must be conducted at BSLMC or its affiliated institutions. Before the committee will consider a proposal, the investigator must already hold IRB approval from a St. Luke's-accepted IRB (BRANY, Baylor, UT or CHI). Projects with clinical application that could improve care quality or safety of hospitalized patients at BSLMC receive highest priority. No career-stage, degree or track restriction is stated.
record.notes: The Roderick D. MacDonald Research Fund is a Baylor St. Luke's Medical Center endowment, administered through BCM's Office of Research IT page, that awards up to $50,000 for one year with five review deadlines annually (2026: Jan 7, Mar 9, May 7, Aug 7, Nov 9). It is open to BSLMC professional staff and associated investigators, and explicitly to clinicians from other institutions whose collaborative project involves St. Luke's staff and is conducted at BSLMC or an affiliate, so a BCM breast medical oncologist practicing at Baylor St. Luke's is a natural applicant. For the PI it is the quickest local source of seed money for a ctDNA/MRD or EHR pilot, a biomarker sub-study nested in an existing trial, or start-up costs for an investigator-initiated trial. The trap is sequencing: the committee will not consider a proposal until a St. Luke's-accepted IRB (Baylor, BRANY, UT or CHI) has already approved the protocol, so the IRB submission must precede the fund application by months, and the budget cannot carry indirects, travel, publication costs or more than $10,000 in salary. The committee gives highest priority to work with clinical application to the quality or safety of care for hospitalized BSLMC patients, so an outpatient breast biomarker project should articulate a concrete care-delivery payoff at St. Luke's. Applications are delivered on paper to the committee chair and the BSLMC Office of Research (Neurosensory Building, 3rd floor). Next step: obtain IRB approval for the pilot protocol now and target the November 9, 2026 deadline; the committee normally meets within three weeks of each deadline.

record.sponsor_full: Rice University Office of Research, Creative Ventures Fund / Educational and Research Initiatives for Collaborative Health (ENRICH)
record.program: Rice and TMC Collaborator Fund (with the Provost's TMC Collaborator Fund)
record.award_text: Up to $50,000 direct costs over 12 months, structured as $25,000 from Rice ENRICH to the Rice co-PI plus a required $25,000 match (cash or in-kind) from the TMC partner institution; no F&A permitted
record.indirects: Not allowed: the program page states no F&A costs are permitted
record.typical_month: Rolling within the Rice fiscal year (FY27 = July 2026 through June 2027); no fixed month
record.eligibility: The applicant of record must be a Rice University faculty member (any discipline) proposing a new collaborative research project with a faculty member at a Texas Medical Center health-related institution; Baylor College of Medicine qualifies as the partner institution. Rice ENRICH funds the Rice co-PI's $25,000 half; the TMC collaborator's institution must provide the matching $25,000, and in-kind support in lieu of cash match is explicitly allowed. No rank, degree, track or clinical-duty restriction is stated on the program page. Projects run 12 months from the date in the award letter with a mid-term report at 7 months and a final report at the end.
record.notes: The Rice and TMC Collaborator Fund is a rolling seed mechanism run by Rice's ENRICH office that pays $25,000 to a Rice faculty co-PI for a new collaborative health-related project with a TMC institution, contingent on the partner institution matching $25,000 in cash or in kind. For the PI, this is the standing low-friction route to a Rice-side partner on an EHR, ctDNA/MRD or imaging-analytics pilot, since Rice supplies the computational or engineering collaborator and ENRICH supplies that collaborator's half of the budget. The PI cannot apply directly: the Rice faculty member is the applicant of record and submits by email to ENRICH@rice.edu, so the first step is recruiting a Rice co-PI and securing a departmental or Duncan Cancer Center commitment (in-kind is acceptable) for the BCM half. The trap is treating this as $50,000 of new money; only $25,000 is external, it carries no F&A, and the project must finish in 12 months with a 7-month interim report. The page states that awards are rolling and proposals are accepted in FY27, and ENRICH's opportunities page says proposals are currently being accepted, so there is no deadline to wait for. Decisions come within three weeks of submission. Past awards have gone to Rice-BCM digital health and health equity projects at $50,000 each, which is a good precedent for the PI's real-world-data angle. The disease-specific fit is low because the fund is generic health research, so competitiveness rests on the novelty of the Rice-BCM pairing rather than on breast cancer relevance.

record.notes: The Chao Physician-Scientist Award is a BCM intramural award, funded by the Ting Tsung and Wei Fong Chao Foundation and run through the ICTR/Office of Research awards portal, giving up to two physicians $100,000 for one year as interim support while they secure a K08 or K23. It is distinct from the held BCM Interim Funding Program, which bridges lapsed extramural support; this one funds the pre-K gap and explicitly asks for prior K critiques and responses. For the PI, an MD-only breast oncologist with clinical duties at BCM, the eligibility gate (physician, primary full-time BCM appointment) is met, and any research angle qualifies, so a ctDNA/MRD real-world data project or an ER+/HER2+ biomarker project could be the vehicle. The trap is the framing: the award is written for "young investigators beginning their independent research careers" who are actively pursuing a K08/K23, so a year-7+ assistant professor who is not on a K trajectory will not read as the intended candidate, and reviewers will expect a concrete K23 submission plan (or a scored resubmission) in the application. The application page returned 404 on 2026-09-10 and no current deadline is posted; the last documented deadline was 2024-05-06 and FY26 awards were announced in July 2025, so the cycle appears to close each spring. Next step for the PI: email awards@bcm.edu or ICTR@bcm.edu to confirm the FY28 timeline and whether faculty beyond five years of appointment are considered, and decide whether a K23 is genuinely on the roadmap before investing in this application.
record.evidence: ICTR index page (orit.research.bcm.edu/ictr/index.html) lists a link titled "Chao Physician-Scientist Award" pointing to orit.research.bcm.edu/R5T80IF3WH2/ChaoAward/Default.aspx, which returned HTTP 404, as did .../ChaoAward/Index (establishes the program is listed by ICTR but the application page is currently down). record.eligibility: Open to current or incoming early-career faculty at Baylor College of Medicine or the University of Houston who are within 5 years of their initial faculty appointment as of the cohort start date (January 1, 2025 for the FY25 call). Applicants must hold a relevant terminal degree (MD, DO, DNP, MD/PhD, PharmD, PhD, DrPH, RN-PhD or EdD), must not have previously won a substantial career development award (K23, K08, VA CDA) or independent award (R01), and may not have a pending K or equivalent federal application at the time of appointment. Scholars must devote at least 75% of total professional effort to the K12 (50% for surgeons with prior approval), with a departmental letter guaranteeing that release time, and must be US citizens, noncitizen nationals or permanent residents. Dual appointees at the Michael E. DeBakey VA require individual consultation.
record.notes: The CTPH K12 Scholars Program is the mentored career-development arm of the BCM-University of Houston NCATS CTSA hub (NIH award K12TR004522, companion to the UM1 hub already represented in the database by the CTPH Pilot Awards). It buys two years of protected time (up to $120,000 salary plus $27,500 research support per year) for early-career BCM or UH faculty who commit to translational science, precision health and health equity, with a core curriculum, mentor training and cohort activities. The program page posts no deadline; the only public call is the FY25 RFA with an optional LOI due 2024-11-08, applications due 2024-11-22 and a 2025-01-01 start, and the inaugural four-scholar cohort was announced in March 2025. For this PI the mechanism is closed on two independent grounds: the FY25 eligibility required being within 5 years of the initial faculty appointment as of the start date, and the PI is in faculty year 7 or later; and scholars must devote at least 75% of total professional effort to the K12, which a breast medical oncologist with clinical duties is unlikely to release. The trap is to treat the program page's silence on eligibility as openness; the RFA carries the binding limits. The PI's realistic use of this program is as a mentor or mentoring-committee member for a junior BCM faculty colleague in breast oncology, EHR/real-world-data or ctDNA work, which builds the mentorship record other awards weigh. If a future RFA relaxes the years-since-appointment window, the record should be re-verified; until then, watch ctph@bcm.edu announcements each autumn and do not plan around it.

record.sponsor_full: Robert J. Kleberg, Jr. and Helen C. Kleberg Foundation
record.program: Medical Research Grant
record.award_text: No stated cap; 2025 medical research awards ranged from $80,266 (1 year) to $1,560,108 (3 years), with most cancer and translational awards at about $1.5M over 3 years. Project support beyond three years is generally not considered. No indirect costs.
record.indirects: Not allowed: the general guidelines state the Foundation does not support indirect costs or overhead allocated to projects.
record.typical_month: March and September (windows open 1 Feb and 1 Aug; close 31 Mar and 30 Sep at midnight CST)
flags: limited-submission: one application per institution per cycle, chosen by BCM internal competition and signed off by the Provost or VP Research
Foundation seeks highly innovative, groundbreaking basic and applied biology; seven-figure awards have gone to established labs, so a year-7 assistant professor will need a strong internal case
finder claim corrected: institutions without funding in the past ten years are refused outright, not routed to a Pre-Request; BCM is funded and unaffected
fall 2026 deadline 30 Sep is 20 days out; the BCM internal slot for this cycle is almost certainly already assigned, so the realistic target is the spring 2027 internal competition
record.eligibility: Applicants are institutions, not individuals: applications from an individual researcher are not considered, and each medical research institution may submit exactly one application per grant cycle regardless of open grants or number of affiliated entities, approved by the Provost or Vice President for Research, with internal competition preferred. Eligible organizations are IRS 501(c)(3) public charities or public universities under section 170(c), and the Foundation currently refuses applications or pre-requests from organizations that have received no Kleberg funding in the past ten years; BCM clears that bar with awards in 2017, 2021, 2023, 2024 and 2025. Priority goes to institutions with a long-standing Foundation relationship, preferably in Texas. No degree, rank, track, career-stage, or clinical-duty restriction is placed on the investigator.
record.notes: The Kleberg Foundation Medical Research Grant is a Texas-priority private mechanism that funds highly innovative basic and applied biomedical research at roughly $1.5M over three years, with two cycles a year closing 31 March and 30 September. It matters to the PI because BCM is an established Kleberg grantee (awards in 2017, 2021, 2023, 2024 and 2025), Rice received $1.56M in 2025 for a breast cancer diagnostic, and cancer biomarker and immunotherapy projects were funded in the same cycle, so translational work on HER2 heterogeneity, endocrine resistance or ctDNA biomarkers is within the Foundation's range. The trap is that this is not something the PI can apply to directly: the Foundation refuses applications from individual researchers, BCM gets one slot per cycle chosen by internal competition and signed by the Provost or VP Research, and no indirect costs are paid, so the department must absorb overhead. The 30 September 2026 fall deadline is open on the Foundation side, but BCM's internal selection for that cycle has almost certainly closed. The PI should ask the BCM Office of Research or the limited-submissions coordinator when the spring 2027 internal call opens (Foundation window 1 February to 31 March 2027) and prepare a one-page concept pitched as groundbreaking biology rather than incremental trial work, since the Foundation's language favors top-tier innovation and its awards skew toward senior labs. Note also that the finder's claim about a Pre-Request route for unfunded institutions is wrong on the current page, which states such organizations are not accepted at all.

record.sponsor_full: Harrington Discovery Institute at University Hospitals
record.program: Harrington Scholar-Innovator Award
record.award_text: Two-year grant with a $100,000 guaranteed award (direct costs only), plus the opportunity to compete for acceleration funds up to $300,000 and to qualify for investment funds typically up to $2MM; awardees also receive a drug-development team, project manager, and regulatory/IP/commercialization support. Up to 12 Scholar-Innovators chosen per year.
record.indirects: None allowed: "Funds can be applied to direct costs only (no institution overhead or indirect costs)." PI salary capped at 10% of the award; no travel, publication fees, or student support; equipment capped at $10,000.
record.typical_month: June (call opens mid-April; 2026 cycle: opened 2026-04-16, closed 2026-06-22)

record.eligibility: The applicant must hold an MD or MD/PhD (or equivalent) and a faculty position at an accredited academic medical center, university or research institution in the US, US territories or Canada, and must conduct the majority of the research there. Each project has a single PI who is responsible for oversight and financial management. No career-stage, age, years-since-training, rank, or tenure-track requirement is stated, and clinical duties are not restricted. The project must be a therapeutic development program (small molecule, biologic, or other therapeutic modality) addressing an unmet medical need with a strong IP or protection strategy; diagnostics or devices qualify only as part of a therapeutic project.
record.notes: The Harrington Scholar-Innovator Award is a national, annual physician-scientist drug-development award from the Harrington Discovery Institute at University Hospitals (Cleveland): a two-year $100,000 direct-cost grant, a chance to compete for up to $300,000 in acceleration funds and up to about $2MM in investment, and a dedicated drug-development team and project manager. It is one of the few mechanisms that requires an MD (or MD/PhD) rather than a PhD, has no career-stage cap, and does not restrict clinical duties, so the PI clears every eligibility line. The trap is scope: the program funds therapeutic development of a specific small molecule, biologic, or other modality with a defensible IP position, and diagnostics or devices only when embedded in such a project. The PI's leading angles (EHR/ctDNA real-world data, investigator-initiated trials, biomarker discovery) do not qualify, and only a novel agent for HER2-heterogeneous or endocrine-resistant disease with institutional IP would. The award also allows no indirect costs and caps PI salary at 10%, which BCM sponsored programs will need to accept. The 2026 cycle closed 2026-06-22 and the 2027 class is announced March 2027; dates for the next call have not been posted, but the pattern is a mid-April opening and a late-June deadline. The PI should log this as a spring-2027 target only if a proprietary therapeutic candidate exists, and otherwise treat it as a low-priority mechanism.

record.program: Directed breast cancer research support (BCM, MD Anderson, Houston Methodist)
record.award_text: Not a published award. record.career_cap: none stated
record.eligibility: No eligibility criteria, RFA, or application process are published anywhere on nobcf.org. The foundation directs its annual proceeds to three standing beneficiaries: the Lester and Sue Smith Breast Center at BCM (currently a named basic-science lab working on aging, metastasis, treatment resistance and endocrine resistance in ER+ disease), MD Anderson (a breast cancer prevention vaccine program), and Houston Methodist's Department of Nanomedicine. Support is relationship-mediated through each institution's leadership and development office, not competitive. A BCM assistant professor with clinical duties is not excluded by any stated rule, but would need the Smith Breast Center director and BCM Foundation Relations to put a project forward.
record.notes: The Nancy Owens Breast Cancer Foundation is an all-volunteer Houston nonprofit (founded after its namesake's death in 2001) that raises money through an annual October luncheon and a Fashion for the Cure event and hands the proceeds to three fixed beneficiaries: the Smith Breast Center at BCM, MD Anderson, and Houston Methodist's nanomedicine department. There is no grant program: nobcf.org has no RFA, no application, no deadline, and no eligibility text, and the foundation's own archive shows the money arriving as luncheon-day checks (2023: $120,000 split three ways; 2022: $165,000). The BCM share has historically gone to one established basic-science lab whose current project is described as work on endocrine resistance in ER+ breast cancer, which is thematically close to the PI's third angle but is already spoken for. The finder's claim that the foundation 'plays a pivotal role in securing federal and state funding' could not be found on any nobcf.org page or the BCM giving page and should be discarded. The trap is treating this as something to apply to; it is a donor relationship owned by the Smith Breast Center director and BCM Office of Development, and any support for the PI would be a directed gift of roughly $40,000 negotiated through them. What the PI should do: ask the Smith Breast Center leadership whether the foundation's BCM allocation is reviewed annually and whether a clinical or real-world-data project could be presented as a second beneficiary before the October 16, 2026 25th-anniversary luncheon, when the year's gifts are typically presented. Fit is modest because the award is small, non-competitive, and currently directed elsewhere.

record.eligibility: No eligibility statement is published. Funded investigators to date sit at MD Anderson, Dana-Farber, Vanderbilt, Duke, Ohio State and the University of Delaware, spanning laboratory, translational and social-science work, so there is no institutional, degree or career-stage restriction in evidence. record.notes: The IBC Network Foundation is a Sealy, Texas patient-founded charity whose sole research purpose is inflammatory breast cancer; its funding page is a ledger of roughly $2.0M released from 2012 through 2026, not an application guide. There is no open call: the foundation issued one formal RFA in 2018 and has since funded by invitation and direct negotiation, with awards documented at $1,500 to $150,000 and a 2026 research grant of $50,000. For the PI this is a pilot-scale, non-competitive-calendar source that fits only if a project is framed around IBC itself, where HER2-positive disease is over-represented and the world's largest IBC clinic sits at MD Anderson across the Texas Medical Center. A HER2-heterogeneity, ADC-response or ctDNA/real-world outcomes sub-study restricted to IBC patients is the natural pitch; a generic ER+/HER2+ proposal will not be funded. The trap is treating the 2018 RFA page as a live mechanism, or assuming indirects are paid. Next step: send a one-page concept to hello@theibcnetwork.org, ideally co-developed with an MD Anderson IBC collaborator, and ask what the foundation is funding in the current year.

record.eligibility: The applicant of record is an organization, not an individual: it must qualify as a 501(c)(3) exempt organization or an equivalent charitable organization outside the United States, so BCM would submit with the PI named as the project lead. The fund prioritizes requests that "contribute to an applicant organization's specific cancer research project or initiative" or to public education programs; no cancer type, degree, career stage, track, or clinical-duty restriction is stated and all US states are served. Funds cannot be used for actual treatment of cancer patients except as incidental to research or education, and may be used for no purpose other than alleviating suffering from cancer through research on its cause, treatment and care, and public education.
record.notes: The Anna Fuller Fund is a perpetual private foundation administered by Wells Fargo Philanthropic Services that makes 5-8 cancer research or education grants a year, averaging $75,000-$150,000 each, to 501(c)(3) organizations for a specific cancer research project. For the PI it is a pilot-scale, no-strings source: there is no degree, career-stage, track, or clinical-duty gate, no cancer-type restriction, and a 2025 award of $150,000 went to a breast cancer research project at Dana-Farber, so a ctDNA/EHR registry study or an ER+/HER2+ biomarker project fits the stated purpose. The trap is that the applicant is the institution, not the PI: the online CyberGrants form is submitted in BCM's name, so the PI must route the request through BCM Foundation Relations and sponsored programs early rather than filing it personally, and should ask Wells Fargo grant administration whether indirect costs are allowable since the page is silent. Applications are accepted year-round but only those in by July 31 are reviewed at the year-end meeting, with decisions communicated by January; the 2026 cycle has closed, so the PI should target the July 31, 2027 deadline and confirm the date on the page in spring 2027. Periodic progress and final reports may be required. Fit is moderate: the award is small relative to a federal grant but well matched to generating preliminary data.

record.notes: Jazz Pharmaceuticals' Investigator Sponsored Trials (IST) programme is a rolling industry portal, structurally identical to the held AstraZeneca, Daiichi Sankyo, Merck and Genentech records: the investigator's institution sponsors the study and Jazz may supply study drug, funding, or both, with amounts negotiated per proposal. It matters to the PI because Jazz owns zanidatamab (Ziihera), a HER2 bispecific already FDA-approved in biliary tract and first-line HER2+ gastroesophageal cancer and now in phase 3 (EmpowHER-BC-303, post-T-DXd metastatic HER2+ breast cancer) and phase 2 neoadjuvant breast trials, plus combination programmes with HER2 TKIs; that makes it the most direct industry route for an investigator-initiated study in HER2 heterogeneity, triple-positive disease or post-ADC resistance not already covered by the held portals. The trap is that the public page publishes neither areas of research interest nor amounts nor review timelines; those sit behind the iEnvision portal login (jazz.envisionpharma.com, pgm=ISR), and the sponsor's breast-cancer interest cannot be confirmed from the public page. The PI should register a portal account, read the posted areas of interest, and email researchgrant@jazzpharma.com with a one-paragraph concept before drafting a full proposal. Because the investigator (or BCM) must act as regulatory sponsor, an IND or IND-exemption path and BCM's clinical research office should be lined up first. The record is 'needs-check' only because the portal-gated areas of interest have not been read, not because of any stated eligibility barrier.

record.notes: NeoGenomics publishes a one-line open invitation for investigator-initiated study collaborations that would benefit from its testing modalities, reached through a Smartsheet contact form on the providers support-resources page; there is no formal program, deadline, review committee or published budget. The relevant asset for this profile is RaDaR ST, a tumor-informed ctDNA MRD assay built from whole-exome data of the tumor, which NeoGenomics markets to biopharma for enriching trial populations and following treatment response and which cites the PENELOPE-B ER+/HER2-negative breast cancer ctDNA work on its pharma page. For the PI this is the cheapest realistic route to add serial MRD readouts to an EHR- or registry-anchored ER+/HER2+ cohort or to a small investigator-initiated trial without buying assays from a grant, and it complements rather than duplicates the held Exact Sciences (Oncotype DX) and Agendia (FLEX transcriptome) records, neither of which supplies ctDNA. record.award_text: No funding. Deliverable is data access: the GENIE public registry (20.0-public, July 2026, >289,000 samples from >242,000 patients) plus six publicly released BPC clinico-genomic cohorts (NSCLC 2.0, CRC 2.0, BRCA 1.0, PANC 1.0, Prostate 1.0, Bladder 1.0).
record.indirects: Not applicable (no funding)
record.typical_month: Registry releases every January and July; access is continuous
record.eligibility: Any researcher may use the data; there is no competitive review, no institutional consortium membership requirement and no fee stated. The page says users must create an account on cBioPortal or Synapse and agree to the terms of access; the terms themselves are on the Synapse pages, which could not be rendered. record.notes: AACR Project GENIE is a publicly accessible pan-cancer clinico-genomic registry, not a grant: release 20.0-public (July 2026) holds more than 289,000 sequenced samples from more than 242,000 patients, updated each January and July, with 21.0-public expected January 2027. The Biopharma Collaborative layer adds deep longitudinal clinical curation, and six BPC cohorts are public today, including BRCA 1.0-public drawn from an early-onset breast cancer cohort. For the PI this is a zero-cost substrate for a computational/real-world-data paper (treatment sequencing, genomic correlates of endocrine resistance or HER2 heterogeneity) that can serve as preliminary data for funded mechanisms already in the database. Access needs only a cBioPortal or Synapse account and agreement to the terms of access; no institutional agreement or review is described on the page, though the terms themselves live on Synapse and were not readable here. The trap: the BPC breast cohort is early-onset and the registry is skewed to institutions doing targeted panel sequencing, so ER+/HER2+ subset sizes and receptor annotation should be confirmed in the data guide before an analysis is promised. Next step is to register, download the BRCA 1.0-public data guide and the genieBPC R package, and scope a subtype question that a mechanism such as a Komen, BCRF or NCI R21/R01 aim could build on.

record.sponsor_full: Academic Breast Cancer Consortium, managed by Criterium, Inc.
record.program: Consortium membership and trial concept development (phase I/Ib/II breast trials)
record.award_text: No award. ABRCC is a CRO-managed (Criterium, Inc.) academic trial consortium, not a funder; value to members is access to industry-sponsored and consortium-designed phase I/II breast trials run under master agreements, with no published grant, pilot, or concept-development dollars.
record.indirects: Not applicable; no grant funds. Trial budgets would be negotiated per study between Criterium, the industry sponsor, and the member institution.
record.typical_month: none
record.eligibility: Membership is institutional, by selection rather than application, and was fixed at consortium launch in August 2014 around sites with an established breast programme, community access, translational capacity, and PIs described as renowned clinical research leaders. The Institutions and Investigators page lists 16 sites (Colorado Anschutz, Thomas Jefferson, CHRISTUS St. Vincent, Ellison Medical Institute, GW, Arizona, Rochester, Northwestern, Swedish, LSU New Orleans, Ottawa, New Mexico, Yale, Stony Brook, Wisconsin, Minnesota); no Texas institution and no Baylor College of Medicine site appears. The site publishes no process for a new institution or individual investigator to join or to submit a trial concept; the only public routes are a sponsor-oriented Request a Proposal form, a generic Clinical Site Registration form, and the director's contact details. The PI could not apply to this as it stands.
record.notes: ABRCC is a real, still-active breast cancer trial consortium formed by the CRO Criterium, Inc. in August 2014, directed by Peter Kabos at Colorado Anschutz, with 16 listed academic and community sites in the US and Canada; it designs and runs early-phase, largely industry-backed targeted and combination studies (TULiP in HR+/HER2+ MBC presented at SABCS 2017; the Personalis B-STRONGER-1 MRD study in TNBC). Its disease focus and its HR+/HER2+ and MRD track record overlap the PI's translational and investigator-initiated-trial angles, which is why it surfaced. It is not, however, a grant: the primary pages carry no award, no application, no deadline, and no concept-submission route open to non-members, and the only public entry points are a sponsor-facing Request a Proposal form and a generic Clinical Site Registration form. Membership is institutional and was set by invitation at launch; no Texas institution is a member, so the PI has no standing to apply or be named. The trap is to log this as an open opportunity or to spend effort on a cold concept submission that the consortium has no mechanism to receive. If pursued at all, it belongs in a contacts list rather than the grant database: an approach through the Smith Breast Center leadership to the consortium director about BCM site membership, or a collaboration with an existing member site on an ADC or endocrine-resistance concept, is the realistic path. No action is recommended for the funding calendar.

record.notes: The Hologic Grant Program is the company's single intake for medical-education grants, investigator-initiated trials, publication support and corporate giving, run through a Versaic proposal portal rather than a scientific competition. record.notes: The Hope Foundation's Secondary Data Analysis Program is a standing, rolling-submission mechanism that pairs a SWOG member investigator with the SWOG Statistics and Data Management Center to run a database analysis on completed SWOG trial data, alone or linked to SEER or SEER-Medicare claims. record.notes: The NIH Extramural Loan Repayment Program for Clinical Researchers (LRP-CR, L30) repays up to $50,000 per year of qualified educational debt for doctoral-level investigators who commit to at least 20 hours per week of clinical research at a domestic nonprofit or government employer. The FY2027 notice NOT-OD-26-081 (released July 13, 2026) confirms the cycle opened September 1, 2026 and closes November 19, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. EST, with awards starting between July 1 and September 30, 2027. It matters to the PI because there is no career-stage cap, NIH funding is not a prerequisite, and EHR, ctDNA/MRD and registry work fits squarely within NIH's definition of clinical research; it is disease-agnostic, so breast or ER+/HER2+ relevance carries no weight in review. The award is personal debt relief rather than research money, so it should be treated as a salary-support complement, not a project grant. The trap is the two hard gates: the PI must still carry educational debt of at least 20 percent of base salary at the time of award, and must be able to document, quarterly, a 50 percent research effort while holding clinical duties; a breast oncologist at 30 percent protected time cannot certify this. A further trap is the exclusion of anyone receiving research support or salary from a for-profit organization, which the PI should reconcile against industry consulting and industry-sponsored trial arrangements. Next step: confirm remaining debt balance and base salary, confirm protected research time is at least 50 percent, then register in the LRP portal, line up the mentor or institutional contact and the BCM business official certification, and submit before November 19, 2026.

record.notes: The Stephen I. Katz ESI R01 (PAR-25-322, reissue of PAR-24-075, open 2025-08-25 through 2028-08-26) is an uncapped, up-to-five-year NIH R01 reserved for Early Stage Investigators proposing a new research direction with no preliminary data; NCI is among the 24 participating ICs. It matters to the PI because the usual barrier to a first R01 for an MD-only clinician, the absence of a preliminary dataset, is inverted here: preliminary data are forbidden, and the review criteria instead ask for a sound premise and a credible justification of feasibility. A pivot into EHR/registry real-world-data methods or ctDNA/MRD analytics, or a biomarker-discovery project in HER2-heterogeneous or triple-positive disease, could be framed as a change in direction from a clinical-trials background, provided the PI has not already published in that exact area. record.notes: The FDA Broad Agency Announcement is the agency's annual, agency-wide contract solicitation for regulatory-science R&D; the Oncology Center of Excellence funds a slice of it and lists oncology real-world data/real-world evidence, clinical trial designs and endpoints/statistical methodology, precision oncology, oncology safety and patient-focused drug development among its FY26 interest areas. The FY26 Stage I cutoff (2026-02-24) has passed and the FY27 BAA is not yet posted; the pattern is a new BAA in December/January, optional early concept papers in early November, and a Stage I cutoff in late February. record.eligibility: Open to investigator-initiated, interventional, proof-of-concept, Phase I or Phase IIA clinical trials of an already-approved drug, biologic, cell/gene therapy or combination in a new indication for any "unsolved disease," conducted at an accredited academic or nonprofit research institution or health system anywhere in the world (start-ups, biotechs and pharma are not eligible). The trial must include AI-generated data as part of its preclinical support and submit a two-page AI Supporting Evidence Form with the LOI. The PI may be either a previously funded investigator or an early-stage investigator with little or no extramural funding (the latter needs a mentor letter of support); there is no career-stage cap, degree requirement, or restriction on clinical duties. CWR funding must be the sole, late or final funding needed to complete the aims, the timeline may not exceed 36 months, and the institution must commit a 10% match if the LOI advances.
record.notes: Cures Within Reach's AI Validation RFP funds small investigator-initiated proof-of-concept, Phase I or Phase IIA trials that test an already-approved therapy in a new indication, where AI-generated evidence forms part of the preclinical rationale. It sits squarely at the intersection of the PI's first two angles: a computational or AI-derived repurposing hypothesis (angle 1) tested in a small IIT (angle 2), and the sponsor's "unsolved disease" definition explicitly covers settings where "many patients develop resistance to the therapy," which maps onto endocrine-resistant ER+ disease. The 2026 cycle is closed (LOI due 2026-06-26, now under review); the 2025 cycle had an August deadline, so the next release is projected for spring 2027 but no date is posted. The traps are financial and structural: the $100,000 budget is really $90,000 from CWR plus a required 10% institutional match, CWR money must be the sole, late or final funding for the stated aims (it cannot be seed money for a larger trial), indirects are capped at 30%, and the sponsor prefers rare diseases and off-patent drugs, so a common-cancer, on-patent proposal starts at a scoring disadvantage. Note also that CWR states it may reject applications substantially written by generative AI. The realistic play is a lean, drug-donated or add-on cohort (for example an off-patent repurposed agent layered onto standard endocrine therapy or an ADC backbone) whose only unmet funding is in the $100,000 range, with an AI workflow diagram prepared with a Rice or BCM data-science collaborator. Next step: watch the CWR funding page from March 2027, line up the departmental match commitment and AI Supporting Evidence Form in advance, and confirm with research@cureswithinreach.org that a breast cancer resistance setting qualifies as an unsolved disease.

record.notes: The Donaghue Foundation's Greater Value Portfolio is an annual national program that funds two-year projects (up to $500,000 plus 10% indirects) testing approaches and tools health systems can readily adopt to improve the value of care; cohorts have been funded every year from 2015 through 2025. It fits the PI's real-world-data and equity angles rather than the ER+/HER2+ biology work: a credible pitch would be a pragmatic test of an EHR- or ctDNA-informed pathway (for example, de-escalating low-value surveillance or imaging in early breast cancer) deployed inside a delivery system such as Harris Health or Baylor St. Luke's, with cost and equity outcomes. The trap is submitting a disease-biology or biomarker-discovery proposal; the program rewards operational tools a health system can use tomorrow, and the applicant must show a formal healthcare-delivery partner or an embedded research unit. There is no stated career-stage cap, tenure gate, or clinical-duty restriction, and the MD-only requirement is met. The FAQ, announcement, and LOI guidance PDFs are hosted on Adobe share links that could not be read, so any per-institution limit or exclusion list remains unverified; the PI should download those documents when the 2027 announcement appears and confirm with the BCM office of sponsored programs whether the 10% indirect rate is acceptable.

record.eligibility: Any researcher may submit a data request through the Vivli platform; the administrator check confirms that all required form fields are complete and that "a qualified statistician is part of the team." Requests then go to the data contributor for a feasibility check and, for most contributors, to an Independent Review Panel or Scientific Committee that judges the research proposal on its merits. No degree, career-stage, tenure-track, or clinical-duty restriction is stated.
record.notes: Vivli is a data-sharing platform, not a funder: a request yields individual participant-level data from contributed industry trials in a hosted secure research environment, with no money attached. It matters to the PI because Daiichi Sankyo, AstraZeneca, Pfizer, Novartis and Lilly are listed members, which is the route to pooled or secondary analyses of the DESTINY-Breast series and HR+/HER2+ registrational trials for questions on HER2 heterogeneity, ADC sequencing and endocrine resistance, i.e. the computational and translational angles. Requests are rolling; the process is an administrator completeness check (which requires a qualified statistician on the team), a contributor feasibility review, and an independent review panel judging scientific merit, followed by training and a non-negotiable DUA executed by BCM. The trap is treating this as a funded award or assuming any specific trial is available: ClinicalTrials.gov entries naming Vivli do not guarantee the contributor will release the dataset, and contributor-specific policies (timing after publication, endpoints, regulatory approval status) were not verifiable from the platform pages. A second trap is cost: the Standard environment is free for 365 days but bills $12/day thereafter, so analysis plans should finish within a year or budget the overage. Next step: search the Vivli catalog for the target NCT numbers, confirm a biostatistician collaborator, and pair the request with a funded mechanism (e.g., a pilot or a Komen/BCRF-type secondary-analysis award) that can cover analyst effort.

Access to banked, non-reserved biospecimens and annotated clinical/outcome data from completed phase 2/3 and phase 3 NCTN trials (Navigator inventory described as over 2 million to 3 million specimens). Investigators receive a feasibility assessment and cost estimate; after CCSC approval they must document their own funding for Group biospecimen processing/shipping fees, data collection/processing fees, and laboratory work within 12 months or specimens return to inventory.

record.eligibility: Requests for NCTN biospecimens from completed NCTN trials may be submitted by investigators in the research community, not only members of the NCTN Groups. The proposal PI must be a CTEP-registered investigator in every submission format. Requests go through the NCTN Navigator (LOI for feasibility review, then a full CCSC Proposal Submission Form with letters of support including one from the study's primary statistician) or directly to the Group bank for trials not in Navigator; if any trial in a multi-trial request is in Navigator the whole request must go through Navigator. Approved projects must document funding within 12 months and publish all results, including negative ones.
record.notes: The NCTN Core Correlative Sciences Committee pathway is NCI's standing mechanism for obtaining banked specimens and outcome-annotated clinical data from completed phase 2/3 and phase 3 cooperative-group trials; it provides no money and instead delivers a feasibility assessment and cost estimate. For the PI it is the most direct route to trial-quality tissue and plasma from completed breast trials (Alliance, NRG, SWOG, ECOG-ACRIN) for HER2-heterogeneity, endocrine-resistance, ADC-response or ctDNA/MRD biomarker validation, and an approved CCSC project is a strong preliminary-access statement inside an R01, R21, DoD BCRP or K-level application. The trap is sequencing: CCSC approval releases nothing until funding is documented, and the 12-month clock starts at the approval letter, so the PI should either hold a funded award that can absorb Group processing, shipping and data fees, or time the LOI so a pending grant decision lands inside that window. The evaluation guidelines favor validation of locked prediction models and pre-specified predictive biomarkers with power calculations and false-discovery control, so exploratory discovery pitches score poorly. The PI must be CTEP-registered (routine for a clinical trialist at an NCTN member site) and must recruit the trial's primary statistician for a letter of support, which usually means engaging the relevant Group breast committee first. Next step is to browse the public catalog at nctnbanks.cancer.gov for candidate trials, then submit a Navigator LOI; proposals accepted at least six weeks before a standing review date are scheduled for that call, with decisions expected about two weeks after review.

record.eligibility: Applicants must hold an MD, PhD, DO, PharmD or equivalent doctoral-level degree, be US citizens, nationals or permanent residents, and be employed by and conduct research supported by a domestic nonprofit or government entity. New applicants must have total qualifying educational debt equal to or exceeding 20 percent of institutional annual base salary and must contractually commit to an average of at least 20 hours per week of qualified research for an initial two years; NIH research funding is not required and there is no career-stage or years-since-appointment cap. Research must fall within a FOCUS area designated by the sponsoring Institute, and NCI's FOCUS areas are data science, computational biology, informatics, prevention, cancer control and population sciences, and human-based approaches to cancer biology, diagnosis and treatment. Ineligible are individuals receiving any research support or salary from a for-profit organization, federal employees working more than 20 hours per week, current IRTA/CRTA recipients, and anyone with a federal judgment lien; only one LRP application per fiscal year is permitted.
record.notes: The NIH Extramural Loan Repayment Program for Facilitating Opportunities in Cutting-edge Science (LRP-FOCUS, L70) repays up to $50,000 per year of qualified educational debt for doctoral-level investigators who commit to at least 20 hours per week of research in an Institute-designated emerging or high-priority area. The FY2027 notice NOT-OD-26-083 (released July 13, 2026, replacing the former LRP-REACH notice NOT-OD-25-094) confirms the cycle opened September 1, 2026 and closes November 19, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. EST, with repayment starting between July 1 and September 30, 2027. It matters to the PI because NCI's published FOCUS areas name data science, computational biology, informatics and cancer control and population sciences, which is a closer match to the PI's EHR, ctDNA/MRD and registry work than the generic clinical-research definition under LRP-CR, and there is no career-stage cap and no NIH-funding prerequisite. The award is personal debt relief, not research money, and is disease-agnostic, so breast or ER+/HER2+ relevance carries no weight in review. The trap is threefold: the PI must still carry educational debt of at least 20 percent of base salary, must be able to certify a 50 percent research effort quarterly while holding clinical duties, and may submit only one LRP application per fiscal year, so L70 and the held L30 (LRP-CR) are mutually exclusive rather than additive. A further trap is the exclusion of anyone receiving research support or salary from a for-profit organization, which must be reconciled against industry consulting and industry-sponsored trial arrangements. Next step: confirm remaining debt and protected time, then contact the NCI LRP scientific liaison to confirm that computational and real-world-evidence oncology fits NCI's FOCUS priorities and to decide between L30 and L70 before registering in ASSIST and submitting by November 19, 2026.

record.notes: RFA-RM-27-012 is the first-cycle Data-to-Model Academic-Industrial Partnership NOFO of the new NIH Common Fund PRIMED-AI program, a UG3/UH3 phased cooperative agreement (administered by NCI on behalf of NIH) to build AI-enabled, image-centered, multimodal clinical decision support tools headed toward Software as a Medical Device. Budgets run to $450,000 direct per year in UG3 and $800,000 direct per year in UH3 over up to five years, with roughly six to eight awards expected; applications are due 2026-10-19 with no letter of intent and no second receipt date. It matters to the PI because the disease-agnostic call explicitly names digital-twin CDS tools that fuse clinical imaging, genomic profiling, and real-world EHR and patient-reported data to model individual response trajectories, which is the PI's top computational and real-world-data angle; an HER2-heterogeneity or endocrine-resistance use case combining pathology or radiology images with ctDNA/MRD and EHR data is a credible framing, but breast cancer is not mentioned anywhere in the NOFO. The trap is the partnership rule: the application must be multi-PI with a designated MPI from a for-profit company that can credibly commercialize medical software, and foundations or research institutes do not count, so an academic-only imaging-AI team (BCM plus Rice, for example) is nonresponsive. A second trap is scope: projects that are not image-centered, that lack a defined intended use and user population, or that propose Phase III trials are listed as nonresponsive, and D2M-AIP is the pre-competitive model-building track while clinical-adoption studies belong under companion RFA-RM-27-013. With five weeks to the deadline and an industry MPI, leadership plan, IP terms, and milestone Gantt charts required, the PI should only pursue this cycle if an existing industry relationship and imaging-AI collaborator can be committed immediately; otherwise it is worth tracking for a possible reissue, since Common Fund programs typically run multiple rounds but this NOFO itself expires 2026-10-20. Next step: contact ODPRIMED-AI@od.nih.gov and the Common Fund program webinar materials, and confirm whether BCM or a Houston partner has a for-profit imaging-AI collaborator willing to serve as MPI.

record.eligibility: Grants go to a Principal Investigator at any not-for-profit research institution anywhere in the world; the institution must accept the charity's Terms and Conditions. record.notes: Worldwide Cancer Research is a UK charity that runs one project-grant round a year, open to PIs at any not-for-profit institution worldwide, funding 1-3 year hypothesis-driven basic or translational cancer research up to £275,000 (typically £200,000-£250,000 over three years). The 2026 round opened 23 February, took submissions from 5 March and closed early once the first 500 applications were in; awards start 1 January 2027 and the site now says only that the next round will be in 2027, so the PI should expect a similar late-February open and early-March submission window but no dates are posted. For this profile the mechanism suits only the translational angle: HER2-heterogeneity, endocrine-resistance or ADC-response biomarker work built on existing Smith Breast Center or Duncan Cancer Center biobank tissue and ctDNA archives, with Rice, UTHealth or MDACC lab co-applicants (up to three, none from industry). It cannot support investigator-initiated trials, patient recruitment, clinical costs or applied real-world-data or equity research, which the handbook excludes outright. Two traps: the charity pays zero overheads, non-negotiable, so BCM sponsored programs must agree in advance to waive F&A, and PI salary cannot be requested. The MD-without-PhD route exists ("other suitably qualified persons, e.g., medical doctors, with appropriate research experience") but is a judgement call, so the application should foreground the PI's laboratory or biomarker publication record and consider naming a senior lab collaborator or department head as co-applicant. Because the round is first-come-first-served, the PI should register on the new grant portal as soon as the 2027 round is announced and line up Head of Department and Authorising Officer approvals before the window opens.

Trials list a dbGaP accession (phs number); trials not yet in dbGaP are not requestable through this route.
record.notes: The NCTN/NCORP Data Archive is NCI's standing repository of patient-level, de-identified clinical data from published cooperative-group trials; since May 2, 2025 all datasets are released through dbGaP controlled access rather than a separate archive site, and as of September 14, 2026 it holds 47,019 patients from 39 trials. It provides no money. The downloadable trial list shows nine breast trials with dbGaP accessions, including TAILORx (10,273 node-negative ER+ patients, phs004260), E2112 (HR+ advanced disease, endocrine therapy plus entinostat, phs004252), MA.17R (extended letrozole, phs004248), E5103 (adjuvant bevacizumab, 4,994 patients), EA1131 (residual TNBC), S0230, ACOSOG-Z0011, RTOG 98-04 and CALGB-70806; no HER2-directed trial is currently listed, so the fit is to the PI's computational and endocrine-resistance angles rather than HER2 heterogeneity or ADCs. The trap is expecting group-level engagement: unlike the Hope Foundation Secondary Data Analysis Program or the NCTN Navigator biospecimen route, this pathway gives raw datasets with dictionaries and no statistician support, so the PI needs an analytic team and a pre-specified secondary-analysis plan. record.program: Academic-Industrial Partnerships for Translation of Technologies for Diagnosis and Treatment (R01 Clinical Trial Optional) - PAR-25-337 (companion PAR-25-338, CT Not Allowed)
record.award_text: Application budgets limited to $499,000 direct costs per year; maximum project period 5 years (up to roughly $2.5M direct over the award). Number of awards contingent on NIH appropriations and meritorious applications; no set-aside stated.
record.indirects: Standard NIH R01; the $499,000 cap is in direct costs, so the institution's negotiated F&A rate applies on top. No cost sharing required. Level of participation and budget details are expected to vary among the academic and industrial partners.

record.eligibility: Standard NIH organizational eligibility: higher-education institutions, nonprofits, for-profits, governments, and foreign organizations may apply. Any individual with the skills, knowledge, and resources to carry out the work may serve as PD/PI; there is no degree, career-stage, or tenure requirement and no bar on clinical duties. Each partnership must include at least one academic and one industrial organization, with industry involved from the beginning of the project. The mechanism supports translation of technologies past proof of principle (enhance, adapt, optimize, validate); it does not fund basic research, commercial production, or phase III trials.
record.notes: PAR-25-337 is the current reissue (of PAR-21-206) of NCI's long-running Academic-Industrial Partnerships R01, which funds the translation of diagnostic and treatment technologies from demonstration of possibility to a status useful in a chosen clinical setting, with a $499,000 direct-cost annual cap over up to five years. It matters to the PI because NCI's stated interests include liquid-biopsy multiomic platforms, minimal residual disease monitoring, and machine-learning models, which line up with the PI's ctDNA/MRD and real-world-data angle; a validation study of a commercial MRD assay in ER+/HER2+ or endocrine-resistant breast cancer, run with the vendor as the industrial partner, is a natural shape for an application. The trap is treating the industrial partner as a subcontractor: reviewers score the partnership itself (complementary expertise, ability to work together), and the technology must already be past proof of principle, so a project built on a new academic assay or on basic mechanism will be judged nonresponsive. Applications that carry a trial are allowed only when translation is the primary motivation, and phase III trials are excluded; a purely observational or retrospective validation belongs under companion PAR-25-338 (Clinical Trial Not Allowed). Next receipt date is 2026-10-05, with further dates 2027-02-05, 2027-06-05, and 2027-10-05 before expiration on 2028-01-08. Recommended next step: identify a willing assay or data-platform company, confirm its investigators will hold substantive roles (MPI is permitted), and contact the NCI program staff listed on the NOFO to confirm that a breast-cancer MRD validation project fits the current portfolio before the February 2027 cycle.

record.notes: PAR-27-069 is an NIH All of Us X01 Resource Access Award that provides stored plasma, serum and extracted DNA from the All of Us Biobank, linked to the program's genomic, EHR, survey and wearable data, rather than money. It is real and open: grants.gov shows it posted 2026-05-19 with a closing date of 2027-03-01, standard NIH organizational eligibility, and no career-stage or track restrictions, so the PI is eligible to lead one. It matters to this profile because it pairs a national biospecimen resource with longitudinal EHR data, a natural substrate for the PI's real-world-data and biomarker angles (for example, plasma-based assays or risk models across a large, diverse cohort) without building a cohort. The trap is that the X01 carries no funds: the applicant must already have, or concurrently secure, an external sponsor (foundation, industry or a separate NIH award) to pay for assays and analysis, and must commit to depositing new data into the Researcher Workbench; the cohort is also general-population, so breast-specific and ER+/HER2+ questions will be underpowered unless framed as risk, early detection or germline questions. The NIH Guide page for PAR-27-069 returned 404, so intermediate receipt dates, an LOI date and the expiration date could not be confirmed; the March 1, 2027 date is the grants.gov close and may be the final of several receipt dates. record.eligibility: The PI must hold NIH Early Stage Investigator status: terminal research degree or end of postgraduate clinical training, whichever is later, within the past 10 years, and never previously successful as PD/PI (including as one of multiple PIs) on a substantial NIH independent research award such as an R01; prior K awards do not disqualify. record.notes: The NIH Director's New Innovator Award (DP2) is the Common Fund's large early-career mechanism for exceptionally creative investigators, worth $475,000 per year for five years with no preliminary data required. The prior cycle (RFA-RM-27-002) closed August 17, 2026, and grants.gov posted the next-cycle forecast (RFA-RM-28-002) on September 3, 2026 with an estimated NOFO post date of March 15, 2027 and an estimated application due date of August 19, 2027. It matters to this profile because the PI may still hold ESI status provided the ten-year window since the end of clinical training has not lapsed and no R01-equivalent has been awarded, and the FAQ confirms the 25% floor applies to research effort rather than total effort, which suits a clinician with substantial patient-care duties. The trap is twofold: any prior substantial NIH award as PI or MPI ends eligibility outright, and a conventional biomarker or trial proposal will not compete; DP2 review rewards a bold, field-changing idea, so a computational or real-world-data project would need to be framed as a paradigm shift rather than an extension of existing work. The award is not track-gated (an independent research position suffices) and there is no institutional cap, but only one application per investigator per cycle is permitted. Next step: the PI should confirm ESI status in eRA Commons now, watch for the NOFO in spring 2027, and start shaping a single-PI concept well ahead of the August 2027 estimated deadline. The $475,000 figure could not be reconciled as direct versus total cost because the NIH Guide NOFO page was unreachable during verification.

record.eligibility: The LOI page states the program is open to academic and community-based physicians and researchers worldwide who wish to pursue independent scientific studies, although the process is framed as empowering members of the Caris Precision Oncology Alliance (POA). Inquiries are screened on data availability, testability of the hypothesis, and lack of overlap with already-approved projects, and all proposals are assessed by the Caris Scientific Review Committee. Baylor College of Medicine and the other Houston institutions do not appear on the POA member list (Texas members shown are UT Health San Antonio Mays and UT Southwestern Simmons), so the PI would submit under the worldwide-researcher route or through a collaborator at a member institution. Approved studies are expected to result in publication, and a fully executed contract is required before data access.
record.notes: The Caris Letter of Intent program is a no-cost, rolling route to investigator-initiated analyses of the Caris clinico-molecular database through the CODEai platform, with support from the Caris research team; it is a data resource, not a funding mechanism. It matters to the PI because the real-world molecular and outcomes data are directly usable for priority-1 real-world data questions and priority-3 questions on ER+/HER2+ disease, HER2 heterogeneity, and endocrine resistance, and an accepted project yields an ASCO-cycle abstract and publication with no budget required. The trap is timing: the September 1, 2026 inquiry cutoff for ASCO 2027 has already passed, and Caris states that inquiries submitted between September 2, 2026 and January 31, 2027 will not be reviewed until February 2027, so a submission now cannot target ASCO 2027. A second trap is institutional standing, since BCM is not on the POA member list; the worldwide-researcher route is stated on the page, but a collaborator at a POA member (nearest Texas members are UT Health San Antonio and UT Southwestern) may improve review odds and access to working groups. The PI should draft a focused, hypothesis-driven inquiry with a clearly testable question that does not overlap approved POA projects, submit it in early 2027 for review in February 2027, and start BCM contract review early because a fully executed agreement is required before any data access. The PI should also check whether BCM's cancer center has any existing Caris institutional agreement that would simplify contracting. This record should be tracked as a resource rather than counted toward funding targets.

record.eligibility: The Research Data page states that TCR provides customized datasets and linkages to researchers under strict guidelines but names no degree, rank, career-stage, institution, or clinical-duty restriction. Any dataset containing personal identifiers or sub-county geography (ZIP code, census tract) requires approval by the DSHS Institutional Review Board or its designated IRB, followed by legal and leadership review, the DSHS Research Executive Steering Committee, and an executed MOU. De-identified record-level Texas data are reachable without DSHS IRB review through the SEER Research datasets (registration plus SEER Data Use Agreement) and the NAACCR CiNA Public Use Dataset (signed Data Assurance Agreement). record.notes: The Texas Cancer Registry is the statewide population-based cancer registry run by the Texas Department of State Health Services; it is not a funding mechanism but a data resource that releases customized incidence datasets, patient-contact listings, and data linkages to researchers. record.notes: ComboMATCH (EAY191) is the NCI precision-medicine platform that ECOG-ACRIN coordinates. Each sub-study pairs a genomically targeted agent with another therapy in patients selected by a genomic marker. It accepts new treatment sub-study concepts from investigators in any NCTN group. For the PI, it is a route to leading a biomarker-selected combination trial with NCI-supplied agents and central matching. An example is a HER2-mutant or endocrine-resistant ER+ cohort, which fits both the investigator-initiated-trial angle and the translational angle. The platform already runs a breast sub-study, EAY191-N2 (HR+/HER2-negative metastatic disease with NF1 alterations). That shows breast concepts are accepted, but it also means a new idea must not overlap open cohorts. The trap is treating this as funding: there is no cash award, and the solicitation post dates from September 2024, so intake should be confirmed as still open. The concept also needs strong preclinical rationale for the combination, plus agent availability through CTEP CRADAs. Next step: confirm NCTN group membership through BCM, then request the LOI template from the ComboMATCH Precision Learning Working Group, preferably with the Breast Committee of the PI's NCTN group on board.

record.notes: PAR-25-235 is the NLM and NIMH R01 for personal health informatics: tools that integrate personal health data (EHR, wearables, geospatial), produce personalized risk assessments, and present actionable insights to individuals. It is the latest in a recurring series (PAR-17-159, PAR-19-072, PAR-23-245, PAR-25-235) and has been reissued about every two years. It fits the PI's computational and real-world-data angle on the patient-facing side, for example a tool that explains ctDNA/MRD surveillance results or EHR-derived recurrence risk to patients, studied with an equity lens. The trap is the dates. The last new-application date under this PAR was 2026-10-05, the 2026-11-05 date accepts only resubmissions, renewals and revisions, and the PAR expires 2027-01-08, so the finder's claim of a January 2027 cycle is wrong. record.eligibility: Open to domestic US organizations (higher education, nonprofits, for-profits, governments) registered in SAM; foreign institutions and foreign components are ineligible. No PI career-stage or rank limit is stated on the page. Required elements are letters of support, NIH-format biosketches (5-page limit) for the PI, co-PIs and senior personnel, and a signed DUA plus IRB approval or determination within 90 days of award. Projects must engage healthcare collaborators or patient representatives and follow a community-engaged, trustworthy-AI design. Engagement of FQHCs, CHCs or medically underserved areas is expected. Applications lacking stakeholder partners are non-responsive.
record.notes: The AIM-AHEAD Consortium Development Program (FAIR-MED, Year 4) funds multidisciplinary AI/ML projects on cancer, cardiometabolic and behavioral health outcomes disparities, using trustworthy-AI and community-engaged design. It matches the PI's computational/real-world-data and health-equity angles, and the Data and Research Core can extract EHR data. The Year 4 round is closed: it was released 2025-04-23, awards were notified 2025-09-02, and the project period runs 2025-09-15 to 2027-09-14. The programs page also lists Year 2 and Year 3 CDPs, so the program recurs, but no Year 5 call was found as of 2026-10-15. The trap is that projects must be disease-agnostic within North Star 3 and need real stakeholder partners such as FQHCs, CHCs or underserved-area clinics, so a breast-specific ER+/HER2+ biomarker project would not fit. A Houston safety-net or community-clinic partner would be needed, and the PI would likely serve as co-PI or clinical lead. Next step: watch aim-ahead.net for a Year 5 call (likely spring 2027) and ask BCM sponsored programs about the institutional (InfoReady) intake.

record.eligibility: The Rice news page does not state eligibility rules, application process, amounts or deadlines. It describes the first-round awards as five paired Rice and MD Anderson teams, each with a Rice PI and an MD Anderson PI. One Rice PI (Ankit Patel) also holds a Baylor College of Medicine neuroscience appointment, but BCM is not a partner institution. A BCM breast oncologist would have no direct route; the only plausible role is as a collaborator on a Rice-MDACC team, which the page does not confirm is permitted.
record.notes: The Cancer Bioengineering Collaborative is a Rice University and MD Anderson partnership that made its first round of seed grants in October 2024. The Rice news release lists five funded projects, each led by a Rice and an MD Anderson co-PI: CAR-T epigenome engineering, a nanocluster plus KRAS inhibitor for pancreatic cancer, engineered Fusobacterium therapy, TRAIL liposomes for colorectal liver metastasis, and cellular plasticity in MDS. None is breast cancer, and none is a computational or clinical-trial project. The page gives no award size, eligibility, application process, deadline or second-round information, so none of those can be asserted. The structure is Rice plus MD Anderson, so the PI at BCM is not a natural applicant. The only plausible role is clinical collaborator on a Rice-MDACC team, and that would need a Rice or MDACC lead to bring the PI in. The PI should not spend effort here now. If wanted, a short email to ENRICH (enrich.rice.edu) could ask whether a second round is planned and whether outside collaborators are allowed. The held Rice ENRICH TMC Collaborator Fund is the better standing route to a Rice partner, and it is a separate mechanism.
record.evidence: The page lists five first-round projects, e.g. "Enhancing CAR-T immunotherapy via precision CRISPR/Cas-based epigenome engineering of high value therapeutic gene targets" with PIs Isaac Hilton (Rice) and Michael Green (MD Anderson). It gives no amounts, eligibility, deadlines or future rounds. It links ENRICH at enrich.rice.edu as the organizing office. One Rice PI, Ankit Patel, is described as also an assistant professor of neuroscience at Baylor College of Medicine.
